item.title: Weekend Getaway Guide: Raleigh, North Carolina
item.description: James Beard–recognized chefs have put Raleigh’s dining scene on the national map, and Michelin’s inaugural American South guide arrived last November, cementing Raleigh as a culinary hotbed. Add world-class museums, transformative outdoor developments, and that unbeatable North Carolina hospitality, and you’ve got a city worthy of a weekend escape. item.title: Q&A: Oscar-nominated director and Atlantan Christalyn Hampton talks about The Devil is Busy
item.description: Christalyn Hampton’s directorial career couldn’t have got off to a better start. Her debut as a filmmaker, The Devil is Busy, which she co-directed with Geeta Gandbhir, has been nominated for the Best Documentary Short Film at the 98th Academy Awards. Set at a women’s healthcare clinic in Atlanta, the film shows a day in the life of Tracii, its head of security. item.title: Rumi’s Kitchen Sandy Springs reopens with a new look and expanded menus
item.description: In March 2025, Rumi’s Kitchen Sandy Springs closed for a planned $3.5 million renovation, estimated to be complete in six months. Nearly a year later, Rumi’s flagship location is reopening after nearly tripling its original budget. New offerings include innovative cocktails and desserts, a selection of water offerings complete with tasting notes, and a glassed-in patio. item.title: Behind the scenes of the Alliance Theatre’s world premiere of Fires, Ohio
item.description: When Beth Hyland first shopped around the script for her play Fires, Ohio, multiple theater companies told her it was unproducible. There wasn’t a problem with the dialogue or the plot; the script, humorous and gripping, had already won both the Kennedy Center’s Paula Vogel Award in Playwriting and the Mark Twain Prize for Comic Playwriting. item.title: In Durham, I found the writing desk that once belonged to Virginia Woolf
item.description: The first time I pass by the desk, I miss it. The four of us are already in the next room when I spot the sign featuring her name: Virginia Woolf. I retrace my steps, followed by my husband, our daughter, and her fiance. Sure enough, there it is: Virginia Woolf’s writing desk, on display in Duke University’s Rubenstein Library. item.title: The Vesper team goes Italian with Trattoria Lucia
item.description: When Trattoria Lucia quietly opened its doors last late year, it filled a gap in Glenwood Park’s dining landscape: an Italian restaurant designed for everyday dining, families included. item.title: Piccadilly To Go on Candler Road is the future of meat-and-threes
item.description: The recently opened Piccadilly To Go on Candler Road in Decatur is a quick-serve model featuring the company’s first drive-through window. Part of the chaotic jumble of fast-food spots, gas stations, discount stores, and other gritty staples of city life, Piccadilly To Go caters to the workaday crowd.
